stem: A 19-year-old man comes to the office due to difficulty seeing and blurred vision, which have both worsened over the past year.  He is a second-year college student pursuing a degree in biochemistry.  His grades are excellent, but he is concerned about the effect his poor vision has had on his classes this semester.  The patient is an avid swimmer.  He weighs 71 kg (156.5 lb) and is 195 cm (6 ft 5 in) tall.  Physical examination findings are shown in the exhibits.  This patient is at greatest risk of death from which of the following conditions?​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌
explanation:
Marfan syndrome is one of the most common inherited connective tissue disorders.  This condition is caused by a genetic defect in the glycoprotein fibrillin-1 and results in structural abnormalities involving the skeleton (eg, long extremities, scoliosis, pectus excavatum), eyes (eg, ectopia lentis), and cardiovascular system (eg, aortic root disease).

The 2 most common cardiac abnormalities in Marfan syndrome are mitral valve prolapse and cystic medial degeneration of the aorta.  In >75% of patients, cystic medial degeneration of the aorta creates aneurysmal dilation at a relatively young age (eg, age <20).  If untreated, this can cause aortic dissection, the most common cause of death in patients with Marfan syndrome.  The second most common cause of death is heart failure secondary to mitral valve prolapse (with regurgitation) or aortic regurgitation (resulting from aortic aneurysmal dilation).  For these reasons, patients with Marfan syndrome should be followed routinely by a cardiologist.

(Choice B)  Breast adenocarcinoma risk is substantially increased in patients with Klinefelter syndrome.  These patients typically demonstrate tall stature with long extremities, but they do not have pectus excavatum or high rates of vision abnormalities.  The risk of breast adenocarcinoma is not increased in Marfan syndrome.

(Choice C)  Overwhelming meningococcal infection is the most common cause of death in patients with terminal complement deficiency (ie, deficiency of C5-C9 proteins, which form the membrane attack complex [MAC]).  These patients do not have skeletal or ocular defects.  Marfan syndrome does not cause immunodeficiency.

(Choice D)  Pulmonary fibrosis is the most common cause of death in patients with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, an acquired autoimmune condition.  These patients do not have skeletal abnormalities like those seen in Marfan syndrome.  The risk of lung disease is not increased in patients with Marfan syndrome.

(Choice E)  Venous and arterial thromboembolism are the most common cause of death in homocystinuria, a genetic syndrome involving impaired breakdown of homocysteine.  Homocystinuria shares the same characteristic body habitus features of Marfan syndrome but patients also have intellectual disability, which is not present in this patient.  Hypercoagulability is not a feature of Marfan syndrome.

Educational objective:Structural cardiovascular abnormalities are responsible for the most life-threatening complications of Marfan syndrome.  Aortic dissection, resulting from early-onset cystic medial degeneration, is the most common cause of death in Marfan syndrome.  Heart failure secondary to mitral or aortic valve regurgitation is also a common cause of death.​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌
